text_full: Simply STUNNING!. I purchased this dress for my teenaged daughter. She is 5’1”, 100 lbs, 32DD, and her measurements are 32.5-24-34. We ordered a size 4 based on the measurements listed by the seller in the product description. The dress we received did correspond to the listed measurements, so I believe the dress to be true to size (if you order based on measurements). My daughter usually wears a size 2, but this dress is not available in that size and because it’s a corset style bodice, I knew we would be able to adjust the tie in the back to hopefully achieve the perfect fit. I’m very happy to report that this dress fit perfectly once we adjusted the corset tie in the back. Also, we have a hard time finding dresses that are large enough to fit my daughter in the bust without the rest of the dress hanging like a sack, but the larger size with the corset tie did the trick without any tailoring required. This dress does has roomy bust, and while I can’t speak for all of the sizes, the Size 4 easily accommodates a D cup. Anything beyond that and you may want to consider sizing up and using the corset ties to cinch it around the waist as we did. On the flip side however, I’m not sure this dress would work for someone smaller than a C cup because the bust would likely be too large and that’s not a good idea with a strapless dress. The way this dress is cut, you can only tighten the bust so much and the rest needs to be filled with...well, you know. I was pleasantly surprised at how nice this dress is. It’s definitely not a costume dress. It’s well made and the materials are not cheap looking. The bodice is fully lined. The skirt is unlined but the dress is made with a nice, thick taffeta and with all the layers of ruffles, trust me when I tell you the skirt doesn’t need a lining. The dress is a nice weight also. It’s light enough to be appropriate as a strapless dress, but heavy enough that it’s feels like a quality garment. I found one flaw (or more likely a skipped step), but it is made in China and the price was quite good so I’m not even that upset. The bottom row of satin ruffles has a split where the two ends of fabric should have been stitched together to create a continuous piece of fabric. If the dress had cost more, if I had more time or if I had purchased it locally I would probably exchange it, but we need it for a dance in 2 days and it’s just not noticeable enough for it to matter. The ruffles are crinkly and gathered and there’s another layer of chiffon stacked on top of the satin that covers it somewhat, so I’d like to think it was just an oversight, but it’s something I’m just going to have to fix myself (I am a skilled seamstress...it’s the principle of it). Even so, I’m not lowering the rating I’m giving this dress because given the price, the overall quality and the fit and appearance, this dress is a real steal and quite a find. If you’re still reading, I’m telling you...just buy the dress! My daughter is over the moon and in love with it, and I can’t help but feel a little smug knowing what a great deal it was! **Note - If my review has been helpful to you, click on the button below and let me know!**

text_full: THE BEST MONSTER. [[VIDEOID:be02a83f5e3bc2dba690e2da1bf4e7f5]] This is my first Seiko Monster. I recently sold my Seiko Alpinist and I was craving a 6r15 movement watch again with a different look. I have 7 inch wrists and I was intrigued by this watch as it was a 42mm case which is my max ceiling for wrist watches. This is a limited release model (1000 made apparently) and only available for the Japanese market which adds some exclusivity to the mix. The dial is a flat dark navy which looks black at first glance. Some people hate the Seiko bracelet....i personally think it looks awesome...but it is a pain to size with the pin and collar system. The bezel has a nice 120 click to it and the overall feel of the watch is substantial and quality. I'm indifferent about the date cyclops....if the crystal ever cracks I'll be installing a domed crystal anyways. I used to own a Seiko SRP637 and for smaller wrists this Monster is the way to go. I love the knurled crown and you can't go wrong with the 6r15 movement. The Lume is crazy...I was outside yesterday and when I came into a dark house it was like having a flashlight on the wrist.....best i've ever had. Mine is running 5 seconds fast but I've only had it for a few days and i'm hoping it stabilizes with wear. If you are in the market for a monster I'd snatch these up before they're sold out.......very little press on these right which is why I snagged it at $520 USD. If you already own a Monster than you are spoiled because you probably paid 1/2 of what I did.....probably less even. This is considered the best reiteration of the Monster and probably the last in my opinion. I wear it around the house, running errands, and it looks good in jeans, shorts, and flip flops. The watch has a presence and people comment on it....I would love to have an orange Monster but I can get an Omega Seamaster for the price that some of these are going for. The Monster was an entry level diver when it came out.....I don't see Seiko going back to 7s26 or 4r36 movements again on these......from now on this is going to be a solid mid level offering in my opinion.....with ridiculous price tags. Get one while you can!

text_full: A beautifully designed, easy to set up and use smart watch. A little on the heavy side, but has great looks and useful features.. I am a huge fan of Skagen watches ever since they were first introduced. The clean, minimalist watch faces and mesh watchbands that are their design hallmarks are not only beautiful, but modern and classic at the same time. My 20-year-old Skagen is as wearable today as when I first got it. Note: This is a hybrid smartwatch, sometimes called an analog smartwatch, as opposed to a fitness watch (this can function as a fitness watch) or a digital smartwatch. It does not have a touchscreen. It is a watch with smart connectivity. This must surely be the most beautiful hybrid smartwatch yet. It connects seamlessly with the Skagen Connect app and whoever designed the interface of the app should get some kind of award for user-friendliness: set up with the app could not possibly be any easier. Syncing the watch to your smartphone is a pretty fun experience because the clock hands spin around to let you know that it has not only connected, but also performed the various other tasks you might want it to do. My iPhone Health app no longer tracks my steps without a third party app to act as a pedometer. It used to, but Apple changed that somewhere along the way and my phone no longer does that alone. The Skagen watch does it without draining the battery nearly as fast as other Bluetooth devices do. I like that a lot! Also, the Bluetooth connects without any trouble whatsoever. I wish all of my Bluetooth devices connected as easily! The watch can be set to track activity and sleep, and it can also vibrate in three different strengths to let you know if someone is trying to call or text you. It will even let you know who it is via a visual cue on the watch face. When I received the watch, I was only able to set this feature for a few contacts. With the last software update, the number of contacts was upped, but do not expect that your entire contact list is going to be accessed. It is only for the people you hear from most often - it's the same as entering "Favorites" on your iPhone. The side buttons can be set for several different functions, such as music control. I have mine set to control the camera "shutter." Since I take a lot of photos with my phone, this feature is very useful - basically a remote for taking photos. It will work as long as a camera app is already open. So far, the pedometer seems to be pretty accurate. Accuracy is an issue for a lot of activity trackers, and I've had some really inaccurate ones. This one is definitely among the better ones. The single thing I do not like is the weight. Although it has a fairly thick profile, which was never part of the Skagen look, I don't mind the thickness as much as the weight. It is quite a bit heavier than a stainless steel Apple watch, even though the Apple watch has a touchscreen. If it were not for the weight, this would be a 5-Star watch. (An additional note here - this is not a "video" screen watch, or a touchscreen watch. It is a smart watch in the sense that it connects to your phone to perform functions available to it via the Skagen Connect app.) If you want a stylish activity tracker that you can wear to work or with a suit, this one is the one to get.

This product works BETTER in my opinion than most overly priced lotions at the salons. It smells great, works, leave your skin moisturized, pleasantly scented before and after tanning, and definatley darker. I can cut down on my trips to the salon with this product AND save myself a butt ton of money! I would also recommend this lotion for beginners as well as advanced tanners who even want to break their tanning plateau. I have been talking about this wonder lotion all day!! You WILL NOT be disappointed in any way with this lotion so PLEASE give it a try and see what it can do for you!

text_full: Love these!. These are exactly what I was looking for! I've used witch hazel before, but it was always out of the container with a seperate cotton pad. I think these are superior not only because they're super convenient, but the pre-soaked pads are also nicely waffle textured so it really feels like it cleans your skin more thoroughly. That's not to say they are too rough though, the formula is extremely gentle and soothing. I have oily skin (very oily unfortunately) so I use toner or facial wipes many times a day to freshen my skin and keep pores clean. Therefore it's easy to over-dry my combo skin or, conversely, if the product is moisturizing it can sometimes break me out. I'm also in my 30's now, so I don't want anything too harsh. These pads are the perfect balance. They don't dry me out in the least. My skin is left super soft, soothed and yet it feels very fresh and cleansed at the same time. These also don't leave a film like some other witch hazel products I've tried. As anyone who has used witch hazel before knows, it doesn't have the most lovely of odors, but it's certainly nothing intense or intolerable and it fades very quickly. It's also nice knowing that there aren't any unnecessary additives or scents. You are left with nothing but clean, fresh, soft skin. I also think it's a great value for the number of pads/jars you get... and they don't skimp on product either... the pads are very heavily soaked in the solution which is exactly how I like this kind of product. Go ahead and give them a try... I think you'll probably love them too! UPDATE: I've noticed my skin actually stays considerably less oily longer after each time I use these, more so than with other products of this type I've tried. Granted it doesn't stay perfectly matte, but it's certainly not the mirror that it usually becomes after an hour or so, which for me is impressive. I can only assume this is due to the fact that although it cleanses well, it doesn't strip your skin and dry it out causing it to respond by becoming more oily again. So this is a great option for my fellow oily/combo skin sufferers! PS -- I feel your pain. ;)

text_full: Womens Vintage Owl Print Scarf Red/Cream. Order was processed and delivered quickly. This is a beautiful flat scarf. I didn't realize it was a pattern of two black outline owls printed on the diagonal of the scarf, so that was a nice surprise, I thought it was just one. The color red is a muted red, and the cream has a very slight touch of peach, some of the owl feathers are printed white. The fabric is a light herringbone weave, which complements the longer feather graphics, and all the edges are rolled and stitched.The graphic of the owls is striking. I like how well they appear just as portions of the wings-works folded in either direction. Somewhere on Youtube was a lady who showed 25 ways to wear a scarf like this, I'll have to find it. It's large enough to fit my broad shoulders just folded. I have one of those scarf magnets that might give a little hold. I don't need it for a day long accessory, it's to cover my bare shoulders and arms on a late spring evening. But it will do for the fall, with a herringbone weave jacket, I'm sure. For a bold scarf design, it is sophisticated.
